clue.text: Became less dull in international cast

parts.note: dull light is dim
taken as written
to cast off skin or hair is to shed it

explanation.surface: Someone loses their sparkle while performing in a cast of international actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a noun for the actors, but it is the verb shed, as a snake casts its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to grow smaller or weaker, so the past tense matches a verb phrase about shrinking.

clue.text: Fool appointed to carry piano

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it inside itself

parts.note: an appointed time is the time that is due
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: An idiot has been given the job of hauling a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to dupe someone is to deceive or trick them, which is to fool them.

clue.text: Heard girl will draw plant

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken, and what is written is a word sounding like it

parts.note: an unmarried girl is addressed as Miss; will is shortened to 'll after a word; to draw a vehicle is to tow it

explanation.surface: Someone overhears that a girl intends to sketch a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' suggests sketching, but here it means pull, as a tow truck does.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic evergreen with white berries, hung at Christmas for kissing under, is a plant.

clue.text: Regularly dismissed once brave Yankee that's fearful

indicators.note: every other letter of the words once brave is thrown out, starting with the first, keeping the rest

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier, formerly courageous and now sent away, has become a frightened American.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy in British use means jumpy and anxious, so it matches being afraid.

clue.text: Dog sleeps upside-down, content in field

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside-down means the word is written bottom to top, that is backwards

parts.note: naps are short sleeps

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside, everything except the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dog sleeps belly-up, happy out in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: Bridge opponents abandoning morning meal for card game

indicators.note: abandoning means the bridge players leave the meal, taken out of its letters

parts.note: elevenses is the British mid-morning snack, taken around eleven o'clock
in bridge the seats are North, South, East and West; East and South play against each other

explanation.surface: Bridge players skip their mid-morning snack to keep playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack of tea and biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevens is a patience game in which pairs of cards adding to eleven are removed.

clue.text: Bitter account detective backed

indicators.note: backed means the word goes backwards

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A sour story from a detective who supported it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, cutting remark or taste can be called acid, as in an acid tongue.

clue.text: Absolve cold king

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A plea to forgive a heartless monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of a charge is to declare them innocent, the same as to absolve them.

clue.text: Sold Freud's bust in German town

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A sculpted head of Freud was sold in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as a statue of Freud, but it is the anagram signal meaning broken.
explanation.definitionFit: This Rhineland city is the capital of North Rhine-Westphalia, a large German town.

clue.text: Comparatively solid sportsman keeping to left of course

indicators.note: one word keeping others holds them inside it

parts.note: a skier is a sportsman on the slopes
taken as written

indicators.note: the left of a word is its first letter, as the word is read left to right

explanation.surface: A beefy athlete stays on the left side of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocky means short and sturdily built, so the comparative means more solidly made.

clue.text: Taking time out, notice problem

indicators.note: taking with out around the time means removing that letter from the word
out completes taking ... out, removing the letter from inside the notice

parts.note: a poster is a notice put up on a wall

explanation.surface: Taking a break from work, someone spots a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' looks like a verb meaning spot, but it is a noun, a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question or difficulty, a problem hard to answer.

clue.text: Characters in dissent pedantically rejected expertise

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters read backwards
the characters in the words are letters found running inside them

explanation.surface: A fussy dissenter's objections dismissed someone's skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adept is being skilled, so the noun means skill or mastery.

clue.text: Pity male swimming for leisure

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: It's a shame the man goes swimming purely as recreation.
explanation.definitionFit: Playtime is time set aside for play and recreation, free time away from work.

clue.text: Scoundrel that is scientist

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A rogue who is also a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie was a physicist and chemist who won Nobel prizes for work on radioactivity.

clue.text: Totally different style of painting involving the French ace

indicators.note: involving means holding the other pieces within

parts.note: pop art is a 1950s-60s style of painting based on popular imagery
les is French for the (plural)
A for ace, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: A painting style featuring a French ace looks entirely unlike others.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite poles are as far apart as possible, so the idiom means completely unlike.

clue.text: Visual transformation of coal pit

indicators.note: transformation of signals the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A coal pit is changed into something you can look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means to do with sight or the eyes, a synonym of visual.

clue.text: Angry minister without house

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a cleric is a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A clergyman with no home is understandably irate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric means bad-tempered, from choler, the bile once thought to cause anger.

clue.text: Gulped down starter of sausage with syrup on

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: syrup is rhyming slang for wig (syrup of figs), so with a syrup on means wearing a wig

explanation.surface: Someone swallowed a sausage as a first course, smothered in syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup of figs, Cockney rhyming slang, gives syrup for wig; with one on you are wigged.
explanation.definitionFit: To swig is to drink in big gulps, so swigged means drank down greedily.

clue.text: Ignore old doddery punter

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters totter into a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to overlook a shaky elderly gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punter' suggests a gambler, but it is someone who propels a boat with a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boatman propels his craft with a long pole, as a punter does.

clue.text: About to engage in base desire soon

indicators.note: one piece engaging in another goes inside it

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics
to long for something is to desire it
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to take part in an act of base craving shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like an adjective meaning low, but it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Erelong is an old word meaning before long, so it is a synonym of shortly.

clue.text: Food to clear off uniform and tie

parts.note: to go is to leave, to clear off
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to lash is to tie down with rope

explanation.surface: Shed your uniform and tie, then eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian stew of meat seasoned with paprika, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Associate bit and cut short Roman emperor

parts.note: a bit of something is a part

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Nero was the Roman emperor said to fiddle while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A colleague bit a Roman emperor and cut him off.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a colleague or ally, someone you are associated with in business.

clue.text: Pub cat underneath an expensive car

indicators.note: in a down entry, being underneath means coming after

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A pub cat hides underneath a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolls-Royce Phantom is a famous luxury model, an example of a costly car.

clue.text: End point brought forward in financial backer's scheme

indicators.note: the end point, the final letter of the backer, is shifted one place nearer the front

parts.note: an angel is a person who finances a theatrical show

explanation.surface: A sponsor's plan has its deadline pulled earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: An angel is theatre slang for an investor in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a scheme or ulterior motive, as in asking what someone's angle is.

clue.text: Windy street chap traverses

indicators.note: the chap traverses the street by spanning it, so the street sits inside

parts.note: a guy is a chap

explanation.surface: A man crosses a blustery road.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather has strong bursts of wind, so it is breezy.

clue.text: Prepare to sail north, intercepting our chap at sea

indicators.note: intercepting means getting in between, so the letter sits inside the others
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Heading north, a vessel intercepts our man out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh anchor and get under way, a sailor raises the anchor before departure.

clue.text: Insensitive type changing sides

indicators.note: the sides are left and right, so L is swapped for R

parts.note: a class is a type or category

explanation.surface: A tactless sort keeps switching allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid and tactless, lacking any sensitivity.

clue.text: Beastly sound from male with rising grief

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: woe is grief

explanation.surface: A horrible noise from a man whose sorrow is mounting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' suggests nasty, but it means made by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cry a cat makes, an animal's noise.

clue.text: One attacking a small kindly person outside LA

parts.note: S for small, as on clothing

indicators.note: one word outside another wraps around it

parts.note: a saint is a very kind person

explanation.surface: An attacker is a gentle soul from outside Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is a person who assaults someone, an attacker.

clue.text: Spirited US boxer versus European

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the American heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: An American fighter faces a European opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and full of energy, one is very much alive.

clue.text: Flirts turned drunk consuming last of Chardonnay

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing another piece inside
turned means the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy flirt is downing the last of the white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like an adjective or an anagram signal, but it is the noun sot.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with someone is to trifle with their affections, to flirt.

clue.text: Torture device like this enthralling doctor and team

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: thus means in this way
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A torture tool, much like this one, held a doctor and his team spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: This device crushed the digits of a prisoner, an instrument of torture.
